description: Canonical key-bundle and canonical-JSON test vectors for Family Beacon. Canonical HERE (docs/FamilyBeacon-Testing.md -> Shared test vectors); consumed by sund-client and, by checkout at a pinned ref, by Sund's beaconsim. Never vendor a second copy. These vectors pin the two things three implementations cannot be allowed to disagree about: the canonical JSON encoding, and the domain-separated bytes an Ed25519 signature is computed over. Spec: docs/FamilyBeacon-Sessions.md.

signing.note: A signature is computed over DOMAIN || canonical_json(payload), where DOMAIN is the ASCII string below followed by a single 0x00 byte. Ed25519 per RFC 8032, so signatures are deterministic and every implementation must reproduce sig_b64 exactly.

canonical_json_cases.name: non-ascii-keys-sort-by-utf8-bytes
canonical_json_cases.note: Byte order, not locale collation. Swedish is a shipping UI language, so the ordering of a/å/ö is not hypothetical.

canonical_json_cases.name: array-order-is-preserved
canonical_json_cases.note: Arrays are ordered data; only object keys are sorted.

canonical_json_cases.name: float-is-refused
canonical_json_cases.note: A float has no single shortest representation every language agrees on, so signing over one is signing over an ambiguous encoding. Nothing signed in this stack carries a float; coordinates travel inside an encrypted envelope, which is sealed rather than signed.

bundle_cases.name: bundle-carries-no-initiation-address
bundle_cases.note: Grant-only reachability (CLAUDE.md decision on bundle reachability, July 2026): the bundle carries key material and no queue sender id, so a device is reachable only by peers a member introduced it to. If a field like sender_id is ever added, this case fails and whoever added it has to revisit that decision.

bundle_cases.name: signed-by-another-identity
bundle_cases.note: The injected-device case: a dishonest host serves a bundle whose identity key it controls. The vouched identity_pk does not match, so it is refused before any signature check.

bundle_cases.name: signature-from-the-wrong-key
bundle_cases.note: The identity_pk field matches what the family vouched for, but the signature was made by a different key. Only a real verification catches this.

bundle_cases.name: served-from-the-wrong-slot
bundle_cases.note: Sund serves bundle bytes from whichever slot the host puts them in, without noticing. device_id is inside the signature so the client does.
